args.title: formatExportFilename() builds the date suffix with at.toISOString().slic
args.body:
File: src/exportUtils.ts

formatExportFilename() builds the date suffix with at.toISOString().slice(0,10), which always uses UTC; it should compute the date in the exporting user's/account's local time zone (e.g. using the existing localHour/Intl.DateTimeFormat-based helpers in src/util/dates.ts) so evening exports in zones behind UTC don't get tomorrow's date.

args.title: In the POST /reports/:id/duplicate handler, the new name is built as tru
args.body:
File: src/api/reports.ts

In the POST /reports/:id/duplicate handler, the new name is built as truncate(`${source.name} (copy)`, MAX_NAME_LENGTH), which for long names causes the generic truncate() to cut the whole string (including the appended " (copy)") down to max-3 chars and append "..." instead of preserving the " (copy)" suffix. The name building should truncate source.name to leave room for " (copy)" (e.g. truncate(source.name, MAX_NAME_LENGTH - " (copy)".length) + " (copy)"), so duplicated reports always end in "(copy)" rather than "..." when near the 120-character limit.

Update slugify (used by formatExportFilename in src/exportUtils.ts) to preserve non-Latin scripts like Greek and Cyrillic instead of stripping all characters outside [a-z0-9] after NFKD normalization; e.g. allow Unicode letter categories through rather than only ASCII a-z0-9.

args.body:
label: feature
file: src/util/strings.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.
src/util/strings.ts's slugify does value.normalize("NFKD").replace(accent marks).toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-"), which only keeps ASCII letters/digits -- NFKD decomposes accented Latin into base+diacritic (diacritic stripped, base kept) but Greek/Cyrillic letters have no such decomposition, so they get replaced by '-' entirely, matching the reported behavior and the existing test expecting formatExportFilename("???", ...) to fall back to "report-...".
